drafts/dev-review--dev.review-39/review..title: Forget a draft the reader has cleared
drafts/dev-review--dev.review-39/review..summary: The listing is now the whole truth about what is held, and a read failure still is not.
drafts/dev-review--dev.review-39/review..comment:
**Start here.** This is the interface, running, with a real review loaded into it. Nothing on this page is a picture.

The pane on the left is the agent's verdict. Every lens it looked through is listed, including the ones that came back clean, each with a line on what was actually checked. Click one and the review filters to it. Click **Two authors** to see what a clean lens is for.

The pane you are reading is the review body. Below it sit the findings, each anchored to a line of the diff. Open the **Diff** tab and the same cards hang under the lines they are about.

Drop a finding you disagree with and it stops being part of the review. Reload this page and it is still dropped, because your decisions are an append-only log and not a page of state. **Post review**, bottom right, is where a real review would leave. Here it goes nowhere and says so.

sections.label: Correctness
sections.body: The change makes `loadAll` authoritative about what the source holds. That is the right call, and it puts weight on a path underneath it that was never load bearing before.

sections.label: Contracts
sections.body: What a function promises its callers, and whether the code still keeps that promise after the change.

sections.label: Tests
sections.body: The commit ships a test with it, which is the house rule. What that test pins down, and what it leaves loose, is the question.

sections.label: Two authors
sections.body:
Clean, and worth showing rather than hiding.

The rule this repository is built on is that the app never writes to a draft: the agent is the only author of the file it wrote, so the two can never race for the same bytes. A change that starts deleting things is exactly where that rule gets broken by accident.

Checked: `loadAll` deletes only from `this._byKey`, which is this app's in-memory projection. The only `adapter.remove` in the diff is in the test, driving the adapter directly to stand in for an agent clearing its own file. Nothing here writes to or deletes a draft.

**A lens with nothing in it is the point.** Hiding it would make this review look shorter and make its thoroughness unprovable. Checked and clean, and not looked at, are different answers.

findings.body:
This makes the listing authoritative about what has been cleared, but the read underneath it is still not.

`_absorb` does `await this.adapter.read(path).catch(() => null)` and then deletes the key. So a bucket that answers one GET with a 500 clears the review from the queue, with the same marks removed and the same row reset that a real clearing produces. The reader cannot tell the two apart.

Everything else on this path is careful about exactly this. `Adapter.poll` skips a round rather than report that everything vanished, and says why: a backend that is briefly unreachable is not a change. `Drafts.load` records `could not be read: ...` as a problem and keeps the last good draft. `_absorb` is the one reader of the three that treats a failed read as an answer.

This commit is what makes it matter. Before it, a spurious delete from `_absorb` was papered over on the next refresh, because the refresh only ever added. Now the refresh removes too, so the wrong answer sticks.

The return was documented as the keys that were read, and is now documented as the keys that moved. The code did not change to match: `_absorb` returns every key it managed to read, and `loadAll` hands it every path in the listing, so the array is still every draft in the source plus the ones that went.

Both callers ignore the value. `app.js` awaits `loadAll()` twice and uses neither result, so nothing is wrong today, and that is the problem: a promise nobody checks, describing precision the function does not have. The next caller to believe it will redraw every row on every refresh and it will look like a render bug.

Either compare against the previous marks so the word is true, or drop the return and the sentence together. The second is smaller.

This proves the case the commit message opens with, and it is the right test to have written.

It does not pin the boundary the change introduces. `loadAll` now has two ways to conclude a draft is gone: absent from the listing, which is what this covers, and a read that failed inside `_absorb`, which is not covered anywhere and now has a permanent consequence. A second test that makes the adapter throw on `read` and asserts the entry survives would fail today, which is the useful kind of test to be missing.

The `MemoryAdapter` is already imported in this file, so standing one up that rejects a read is a few lines.

qa.note: Nothing was driven. The change is in a projection with no rendering of its own, and the observable difference is a queue row that keeps its ready dot after a draft is cleared, which needs a source, a cleared draft and a backgrounded tab to reproduce honestly. Read instead: `Adapter.poll` and `Drafts.load` for how the other two readers of the same listing handle an unreachable backend, and both `loadAll` call sites in `app.js` to check what the return value is used for.
